base.prose:
Comparison of the Uganda routine schedule with the generic WHO scheduling
logic in the [WHO Immunization implementation guide](https://smart.who.int/immunizations)
(libraries `IMMZD18S*Logic`). "Same" means the Uganda rule falls within the
WHO recommendation; the remaining rows are the adaptations this guide makes.

| Vaccine | WHO (generic) | Uganda | Adaptation |
|---|---|---|---|
| BCG | 1 dose at birth | 1 dose at birth | Same |
| Hepatitis B birth dose | At birth; overdue after 24 hours; upper limit left to Member States | At birth, ideally within 24 hours, not after 7 days | Upper limit set to 7 days |
| OPV0 (bOPV birth dose) | At birth; IG expiration 1 week | At birth | WHO 1-week expiration kept ([open question](open-questions.html)) |
| OPV1–3 | 3 bOPV doses from 6 weeks, at least 4 weeks apart | 6, 10, 14 weeks, at least 4 weeks apart | Same, with fixed scheduled ages |
| IPV | IPV1 from 14 weeks, IPV2 at least 4 months later | IPV1 at 6 weeks, IPV2 at 14 weeks, at least 4 weeks apart | Earlier IPV1 and shorter interval |
| DTP-HepB-Hib | 3 primary doses from 6 weeks, at least 4 weeks apart; 3 diphtheria–tetanus boosters (12–23 months, 4–7 years, 9–15 years) and a pertussis booster (1–6 years) | 3 primary doses at 6, 10, 14 weeks; no childhood boosters | Boosters not in the Uganda schedule |
| PCV | 3p+0 or 2p+1 | 3p+0 at 6, 10, 14 weeks | 3p+0 chosen |
| Rotavirus | From 6 weeks, at least 4 weeks apart, number of doses by product; IG expiration 24 months | 3 doses at 6, 10, 14 weeks; not after 2 years | 3-dose product schedule |
| Measles-rubella | MCV1 at 9 months (12 months in low transmission settings); MCV2 from 15 months | MR1 at 9 months, MR2 at 18 months | MR2 at 18 months |
| Yellow fever | 1 dose from 9 months in endemic areas | 1 dose at 9 months, nationwide | Same |
| Malaria | 4 doses, first from 5 months, at least 4 weeks apart; dose 4 about 12–18 months after dose 3 | 6, 7, 8 and 18 months | First dose at 6 months; dose 4 at 18 months of age (about 10 months after dose 3 when on time) |
| HPV | Single dose from 9 years (9–14 primary target; up to 20 years) | 1 dose for girls at 10 years | Scheduled age 10 years; WHO upper age kept ([open question](open-questions.html)) |
| Td, women of child-bearing age | Tetanus-diphtheria in pregnancy (IG libraries `IMMZD18SDTPPregnancy*`) and childhood/adolescent boosters | 5 doses for women aged 15–49: first contact, +1 month, +6 months, +12 months, +12 months | Uganda 5-dose schedule for all women of child-bearing age |
{:.grid}

dose, yellow fever and MR2 as *newly introduced*, and malaria and HPV as *yet to
be introduced* at the time of the presentation. The Ministry of Health poster
includes malaria and single-dose HPV in the routine schedule.

Test patients follow the WHO DAK's own layout: one directory per Logic library,
`input/tests/plandefinition/<Library>/<Library>.yaml`, turned into FHIR test
bundles by WHO's `tools/node/makeExample.js` (`npm run logic:examples`; every
file is built on each pull request). Each library's `Test Validation`
expression names, per test patient, the output that should hold, as the WHO
libraries do.

| Library | Test patients | Checks |
|---|---|---|
| IMMZD18SHepatitisBBirthDoseLogic | UGHepB01, UGHepB02 | birth dose due and expiring at 7 days; complete when given on day 3 |
| IMMZD18SPolioBOPVPlusIPVLogic | UGPolio01, UGPolio02 | IPV 1 due at 6 weeks; IPV 2 due at 14 weeks |
| IMMZD18SDTPOnTimeStartLogic | UGDTP01, UGDTP02 | DTP 1 at 6 weeks; no booster after the primary series |
| IMMZD18SMeaslesOngoingTransmissionLogic | UGMR01 | MCV2 due at 18 months |
| IMMZD18SMalariaLogic | UGMal01, UGMal02 | dose 1 at 6 months; dose 4 at 18 months |
| IMMZD18SHPVSingleDoseLogic | UGHPV01, UGHPV02 | girls at 10 years; not boys |
| IMMZD18SDTPTdWCBALogic | UGTd01–UGTd03 | Td 1 at first contact; Td 3 after Td 2; not men |
{:.grid}

The CQL is compiled by the IG build (`fhirbuild.yml`, the WHO path). The WHO DAK
toolchain has no runner that executes `Test Validation` on each change; the
WHO checklist runs it by hand. That gap is reported to the platform rather than
filled with a script in this repository.

/*
 * Library: IMMZD18SHPVSingleDoseLogic (IMMZ.D18.S.Single-dose schedule)
 * Schedule Table: Alternative single-dose schedule

 * Uganda adaptation of the WHO library of the same name: the definitions marked
 * 'Uganda' follow the Uganda copy of the DAK workbook
 * (input/decision-logic/IMMZ DAK_decision-support logic.xlsx), citing L1 P10, S13.
 */
library IMMZD18SHPVSingleDoseLogic

using FHIR version '4.0.1'
include FHIRHelpers version '4.0.1'

include WHOCommon called WC

include IMMZCommon called Common
include IMMZConcepts called Concepts

include IMMZEncounterElements called IE
include IMMZD2DTHPVEncounterElements called Encounter

parameter Today Date default Today()


context Patient


/*
@output: Human papillomavirus (HPV) dose 1
@description: Provision of the HPV dose 1
@trigger: Child's birth
@pseudo: 
@triggerDate: "Date of birth"
*/
define "Human papillomavirus (HPV) dose 1":

# Stage 3 of smart-guideline-end-to-end: which existing DAKs the Uganda L2 builds on.
# One row per candidate (rejected ones included), with the fields the skill names: packageId,
# version, uri (cat-harness DependsOnRecord), publisher, evidence (the L1 KG nodes that point at
# it), decision (reuse | adapt | extend | reject), reason and, per kept component, toolchain:
# how the upstream produces it, which stages 4 and 6 then use. Authored by an agent; the decision is
# the agent's RECOMMENDATION and goes ahead under the QA rule. Adjudicated by the programme manager
# and the business analyst (review requested). Each kept decision-logic table also names its
# PlanDefinition id (planDefinition), so tools find it without matching titles.
$schema: sg-l2-dependencies/draft
candidates:
  - packageId: smart.who.int.immunizations
    version: current
    uri: http://smart.who.int/immunizations
    publisher: WHO
    decision: adapt
    reason: >-
      The WHO immunization DAK covers every vaccine on the Uganda schedule; Uganda changes the
      schedule and catch-up rules and adds national requirements, so its scheduling decision
      logic is adapted and the rest reused or extended.
    evidence:
      - library/l1-recommendation-scenarios/uganda/candidates/*/scenario-candidates.l2.json — 49 of 53 scenarios realised by IMMZ.C or IMMZ.D of this DAK
    components:
      healthInterventions: {decision: extend, reason: "Add the Uganda interventions (HI-UG-*) named by the authored L1."}
      personas: {decision: reuse, reason: "All 53 scenario candidates map to its personas (health worker, caregiver); no Uganda-specific persona is printed in the sources."}
      userScenarios: {decision: extend, reason: "Add the 53 Uganda scenario candidates (IMMZ.UG.Poster.*, IMMZ.UG.UNEPI.*)."}
      businessProcesses: {decision: reuse, reason: "IMMZ.A-I reused unchanged. Four statements have no process (AEFI reporting, caregiver health education, vitamin A, deworming); extending the process set is review item 6 and is not drawn until decided."}
      dataElements: {decision: reuse, reason: "The vaccine value sets and dose data elements cover the Uganda schedule. Data elements for vitamin A and deworming wait on review item 6."}
      decisionLogic:
        decision: adapt
        reason: >-
          The WHO DAK already offers a scheduling table (IMMZ.D18.S.*) for every vaccine on the
          Uganda schedule, and leaves overdue and expiry "to be determined by Member States". Uganda
          is an edited copy of the WHO decision-support workbook: the tables listed under `tables`
          are reused unchanged from the dependency, adapted cell by cell (each changed cell cites
          its L1 key), or extended with a new table. Contraindication tables (IMMZ.D5.DT.*) and the
          eligibility tables (IMMZ.D2.DT.*) are reused unchanged.
        toolchain: >-
          WHO's own: the DAK workbook input/decision-logic/IMMZ DAK_decision-support logic.xlsx
          (Uganda copy), converted per table by litlfred/smart-immunizations tools/node/
          processDTSchedule.js (CQL, Library FSH, PlanDefinition FSH), then the CQL completed from
          the pseudocode as tools/antigenchecklist.md prescribes. The hand-written YAML tables,
          DMN builder and input/dmn/UG.D18.S.*.dmn are retired.
